name: favourite-typed-url-opens-a-new-tab
description:
A favourite's tab is pinned to the site its tile names. Typing another site's URL in the address bar used to navigate that tab away, which left the tile bound to a page it does not name and cost the user the favourite in one keystroke. A URL on the SAME site is that site's own navigation and still moves the tab.

THE FIXTURE IS THE DETECTOR. Its favourite (favicon-page.html) is deliberately NOT the space's startup tab. A live tab already on the favourite's URL is activated by URL and never claimed, and an unclaimed tab is not a favourite's tab as far as the address bar can tell - so a fixture that opened with the page already showing would prove nothing. The startup tab is edit-focus-field.html, the control row.

CROSS-SITE ON ONE SERVER. The fixture server answers on 127.0.0.1:8000 and on localhost:8000, and those two are different sites by the eTLD+1 rule the decision uses - neither host has a registry, so the hosts compare whole. That gives a genuinely cross-site pair whose page still loads, with no network and no second server.

ROW COUNTS. The Rust core hides a row whose URL is a favourite's, so the favourite's own tab never joins the list (favourite-is-not-a-tab-row). One row at rest is the control; the second is the tab the cross-site submission opens. The tile's binding is read as data-fav-tab, which MergeFavoriteClaims writes from the claim the tab carries - the tile paints as bound off exactly that.

actions.note: first paint, and the sidebar announces itself
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot

The only favourite tile, at a-favourite-click-reuses-its-tab's own coordinates - one favourite and the same 280pt sidebar, so the first cell sits in the same place. This click is what OPENS and CLAIMS the tab everything below is about.

VACUITY GUARD. Only OpenFavoriteTab stamps the claim, and only a claimed tab can take the favourite path in the address bar. Without this a click that missed the tile would leave every reading below describing an ordinary tab.

the control row alone. The favourite's own tab is open by now and is NOT one of these - that is the core's rule, and it is why the count below moves by exactly one.

actions.expression: (() => { const bar = document.querySelector('#sbUrl'); if (!bar) { return 'no row'; } bar.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, view: window})); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: Dispatched on the row rather than aimed by coordinate. The old click at 140,70 stopped landing when the sidebar layout moved, which is the same drift prompt-grows-out-of-the-address-row already records against its own plan's x/y. sidebar.js reads e.target.closest('#sbUrl'), which a bubbling synthetic click satisfies the same as a real one.

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.cbcard'); if (!c) { return 'no card'; } return c.classList.contains('cbanchored') ? 'anchored' : 'centred'; })()

assertions.desc: the address row was there to click, so a later /commandbar miss is the palette's fault and not a stale coordinate
the row was there for the same-site submit too
the favourite tile was there for the second click, so a missing activation vlog is the feature's
Liveness, and a guard against a click landing somewhere that spawned a window.
VACUITY GUARD: the tile really was bound before the typing, so losing the binding was something this run could have measured.
VACUITY GUARD: the list starts at the control row, so the count below is a move rather than an absolute nobody checked.
VACUITY GUARD: the row click really opened the palette on the row, so the URL below was typed into a field rather than into nothing.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: command bar opened a new tab beside the favourite's
assertions.desc: THE ASSERTION, from the native side: the decision took the new-tab branch rather than loading the URL into the tab in front.
and the sidebar shows it - one more row than the run started with. Before the fix the count stayed at 1, because the URL went into the favourite's tab, whose row the core hides.
The tile still points at its tab. A navigated-away favourite loses this, and its next click opens another copy.
and the second click opened it again, so the same-site URL was typed into a field too
A URL on the favourite's own site still moves its tab. Without this the run would pass on a build that answers 'new tab' to everything.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: command bar opened a new tab beside the favourite's
assertions.desc: and it moved that tab INSTEAD of opening another one. The ceiling is what pins it - the presence assertion above passes just as well on a build that opens a tab for every submission.
